title: App scaffold, CI, and live deploy pipeline

history.detail:
PASS: AUDITED COMMIT fe7f2db (clean tree; audited content == committed content). Sprint file re-read fresh from docs/sprints/2-in-progress/ immediately before this verdict.

VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, NOT BY READING:
- Clean checkout of fe7f2db extracted via git archive, npm ci (exit 0, 0 vulnerabilities), then CI order: typecheck exit 0, lint exit 0, test exit 0 (4 files / 9 assertions). Also confirmed next-env.d.ts is gitignored and ABSENT from a clean checkout, and typecheck still passes without it - CI runs typecheck before build, so that ordering was a real risk and it holds.
- Req 5/6 mechanism PROVEN, this was the one non-obvious decision and Dev asked for scrutiny. Build output confirms the premise: / is Static (o), /api/health is Dynamic (f). Built with VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA=abcdef12..., then started the server with the env var UNSET at runtime: page rendered abcdef1 and /api/health returned abcdef1. Inline reaches both a prerendered page and a dynamic Route Handler with zero runtime env.
- FALSIFICATION TEST: built with NO VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA to exercise the new Date().toISOString() fallback, on the theory that next.config.ts loading more than once per build would give page and API different timestamps - reintroducing the same bug in the fallback branch. Hypothesis FALSIFIED: both returned 2026-09-03T04:20:06.464Z. Config loads once, value inlined once. Fallback branch is sound.
- COUNTERFACTUAL: rebuilt with getBuildId() reading process.env.VERCEL_GIT_COMMIT_SHA directly (the approach Dev rejected). Page served abcdef1, API served dev-local. MISMATCH. The bug is real, the fix is earned complexity, not over-engineering. This is exactly the sprint's named risk (green deploy serving a stale build) and exactly what LiveQA's matching criterion would have caught in production.

REQUIREMENTS: 1 MET (strict + noUncheckedIndexedAccess, tsc clean). 2 MET (vitest, 9 real assertions on fallback logic/response shape/render, no true===true). 3 MET (flat config, clean). 4 PARTIAL-BY-DESIGN (URL in README.md:3; actual deploy wiring is not statically verifiable and is deferred to LiveQA's third criterion). 5 MET. 6 MET. 7 MET (server-only marker, no NEXT_PUBLIC_ anywhere, no client components at all, .env* ignored with .env.example un-ignored). 8 MET (placeholder line gone, standards describe what was actually built).

FINDINGS - NONE BLOCKING:
1. [MEDIUM, FORWARD-LOOKING] next.config.ts's env block bypasses BOTH documented secret protections. CLAUDE.md's secrets convention is server-only + no NEXT_PUBLIC_ prefix, but env: in next.config inlines into any bundle that references the value, regardless of variable name and regardless of the server-only marker. Verified NEXT_BUILD_ID does NOT currently leak (grep of .next/static is empty) - but only because it is referenced solely from a server-only module. Req 7 exists specifically to set the pattern before Sprint 4 lands an LLM API key, and the convention as written does not cover the mechanism this sprint just introduced. Add a line to CLAUDE.md's secrets section: never put a secret in next.config.ts's env block. Cheap now, expensive in Sprint 4.
2. [LOW] .env.example never names NEXT_BUILD_ID, which lib/build-info.ts:22 actually reads. The acceptance criterion says every variable the code reads, not a subset. It is build-injected rather than user-supplied so a placeholder line would mislead, but a named prose entry costs one line.
3. [LOW] The getBuildId unit tests exercise runtime process.env reads; production uses build-time inlining. Those tests structurally CANNOT catch a failure of the inlining mechanism the whole design rests on. Not a defect - but nobody should read those 9 green assertions as covering Req 5/6's real invariant. My build-and-serve runs cover it now; LiveQA's page-vs-API match is the durable gate.
4. [INFO] Lint ignores scripts/**. Verified legitimate, not hidden app defects: unignoring produces 27 errors, all no-require-imports on pre-existing CommonJS launcher tooling that predates this sprint. Correct call. Note that scripts/ is now lint-uncovered.
5. [INFO] Next 15->16.3.4 and Vitest 2->4 major bumps made unprompted to clear 7 vulns. Disclosed honestly by Dev, 0 vulns confirmed on clean npm ci. Next 16 is new; acceptable on a scaffold sprint where nothing depends on it yet.

SCOPE: clean. No math, auth, or DB. globals.css is legibility-only, within bounds. No unrequested feature code.
ERROR HANDLING: no I/O exists yet, no bare catches, nothing swallowed. N/A this sprint.
SECURITY: no secrets, no user input, no injection surface, all server components.

The build-id reasoning Dev flagged for scrutiny is correct and I proved it three ways. Ship it.

CONDITIONAL: LIVE TEST — https://mygame-black-mu.vercel.app — 2026-09-02 — real Chrome (Playwright-driven, headless, system Chrome 1280x800 + 390x844) + curl. Deployed buildId served: 4194c8c.

VERDICT: CONDITIONAL PASS. The deployed product is sound and every LiveQA acceptance criterion passed. One confirmed documentation defect blocks close: the live URL recorded in the repo is wrong and serves a DIFFERENT application.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA ===
AC1 page renders app name + build identifier — PASS. Real browser, not curl. Rendered body innerText verbatim: "MyGame\n\nBuild: 4194c8c". h1 count=1, text "MyGame", isVisible=true. Build element [data-testid=build-id] visible=true, computed {display:block, visibility:visible, opacity:1, color:rgb(0,0,0), fontSize:16px, w:1216, h:18}. Identifier string I actually saw: 4194c8c. Zero pageerrors, zero failed requests, zero non-2xx subresources. Screenshot captured.

AC2 /api/health 200 with identifier MATCHING the page — PASS. Body verbatim, 10 requests: {"status":"ok","buildId":"4194c8c"} every time. Also fetched from INSIDE the browser session on the loaded page: 200, same body, page code text 4194c8c === api buildId 4194c8c, MATCH. This is the sprint's named risk (page and API from different builds) and it does not reproduce.

AC3 deployed identifier corresponds to the commit Pipeman shipped — PASS, with a nuance recorded deliberately. last_shipped_commit is fe7f2db; the live buildId is 4194c8c (the ship-bookkeeping commit, which is tip of main). These are NOT the same string, so I verified the substance rather than the label: git diff fe7f2db..4194c8c touches exactly one file, docs/sprints/state/sprint-1.json (+24/-6). Diff of everything EXCLUDING docs/sprints is EMPTY — application code at 4194c8c is byte-identical to the audited commit. The build is not stale, it is one bookkeeping commit newer with identical app code, which proves the pipeline IS wired to main (it auto-deployed the bookkeeping push). Criterion intent (catch a stale build) is satisfied. Flagging for Master Controller: Req 5/6's identifier will routinely show the bookkeeping commit, not the audited one, so future sprints should expect this offset rather than read it as a stale deploy.

=== BLOCKING ISSUE ===
1. [HIGH — blocks close] The recorded live URL is wrong AND serves a foreign application. README.md:3 "**Live:** https://mygame.vercel.app" and CLAUDE.md:319 "**Live URL:** https://mygame.vercel.app", both verified at deployed commit 4194c8c and on disk now. The real URL is https://mygame-black-mu.vercel.app.
   This is not a dead link, which is what makes it serious. GET https://mygame.vercel.app/ returns HTTP 200, 3813 bytes, server: Vercel, of an unrelated raw-HTML canvas game — visible source contains "var myGamePiece", "const MOVEMENT_STEP = 10", "const RESIZE_VERTICAL_STEP = 5", a <canvas> style block, no <title>, and zero occurrences of any build identifier. GET https://mygame.vercel.app/api/health returns HTTP 404 "The page could not be found / NOT_FOUND".
   Impact on this sprint's own requirements: Req 4 says the URL is recorded "so LiveQA can find it without asking" — I could not; Pipeman had to hand me the real URL, which is the exact failure Req 4 exists to prevent. Req 8 says CLAUDE.md must "describe what was actually built, not what was planned" — it describes a URL this project never owned. Both unmet as written. A future role following the documented URL gets a 200 and a working-looking page belonging to someone else, and would have no signal anything is wrong.
   FIX: change both README.md:3 and CLAUDE.md:319 to https://mygame-black-mu.vercel.app. Then Pipeman re-ships and I re-test. Not mine to edit.

=== NON-BLOCKING FINDINGS ===
2. [LOW] GET /favicon.ico and /apple-touch-icon.png both return HTTP 404. Produces a console error on every page load, verbatim: "[error] Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 ()". No requirement covers a favicon; noting it because it is the only console noise on the page and will otherwise be mistaken for a real error by whoever tests next.
3. [INFO] Second Vercel project "mygame1" is hooked to this same repo (reported by Pipeman, not independently verified by me — outside browser scope). Not the documented target. Recommend unlinking so it cannot later deploy a competing build under a confusable name; this sprint already demonstrates the cost of an ambiguous URL.

=== ROBUSTNESS / BREAK ATTEMPTS — all held ===
- 3 runs in FRESH browser contexts (cold cache, cache-busted): innerText identical all 3, "MyGame\n\nBuild: 4194c8c", 0 pageerrors each.
- 4 consecutive hard reloads: innerText unchanged, 0 pageerrors.
- 5 paired page-vs-API cache-busted runs: page 4194c8c / api 4194c8c on every pair, no drift. Page served x-vercel-cache: HIT (statically prerendered), API x-vercel-cache: MISS (dynamic) — the two are served by different mechanisms and still agree, which is the strongest form of this check.
- Unsupported methods on /api/health: POST/PUT/DELETE all 405, HEAD 200. Correct.
- Unknown routes: /no-such-page 404, /api/nope 404. 404 page renders properly in browser: "404\nThis page could not be found."
- Mobile 390x844: scrollWidth 390 === clientWidth 390, no horizontal overflow, content renders identically.
- HTTPS enforced, strict-transport-security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload.

RECOMMENDATION: Fix the URL in README.md:3 and CLAUDE.md:319 (one line each, Reqs 4 and 8), re-ship, and I will re-verify. Nothing in the deployed application itself needs to change — the build-identifier mechanism QA1 proved statically holds up live under every attempt I made to break it.

CONDITIONAL: RE-TEST (live_test_round 2) — https://mygame-black-mu.vercel.app — 2026-09-02 — real system Chrome driven by playwright-core 1.62.1 (headless, 1280x800 + 390x844 mobile) + curl. Deployed buildId served: 4194c8c.

VERDICT: CONDITIONAL PASS, UNCHANGED FROM ROUND 1. Re-tested on explicit request. NOTHING WAS SHIPPED BETWEEN ROUND 1 AND THIS RUN — local and remote main are both 4194c8c, no reship event in history, working tree clean except the uncommitted round-1 state file. The round-1 blocking defect was never fixed and it reproduces live. This verdict is a re-confirmation, not new information.

=== BLOCKING ISSUE (STILL OPEN, UNCHANGED) ===
1. [HIGH — blocks close] The recorded live URL is wrong AND serves a foreign application. Verified on disk RIGHT NOW: README.md:3 '**Live:** https://mygame.vercel.app' and CLAUDE.md:319 '**Live URL:** https://mygame.vercel.app'. The real URL is https://mygame-black-mu.vercel.app.
   NEW EVIDENCE THIS ROUND — I loaded the documented URL in a REAL BROWSER, not just curl (round 1 only had curl on this): GET https://mygame.vercel.app/ returns HTTP 200, rendered body innerText verbatim 'UP\n\nLEFT RIGHT\n\nDOWN', document.title is the EMPTY STRING, 1 <canvas> element present, 0 [data-testid=build-id] elements. curl confirms 3813 bytes, server: Vercel, and marker counts in source: myGamePiece x11, MOVEMENT_STEP x5, RESIZE_VERTICAL_STEP x3, and ZERO occurrences of '4194c8c', 'MyGame', or 'data-testid'. GET https://mygame.vercel.app/api/health returns HTTP 404 'The page could not be found / NOT_FOUND'.
   It renders as a real, working, playable page with directional controls. Anyone following the documented URL sees a live site that looks fine and has no signal it is the wrong application. That is what makes this worse than a dead link.
   Req 4 ('recorded so LiveQA can find it without asking') and Req 8 ('CLAUDE.md describes what was actually built') both remain unmet as written.
   FIX: README.md:3 and CLAUDE.md:319 -> https://mygame-black-mu.vercel.app. One line each. Not mine to edit.

=== ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA — ALL PASS AGAINST THE REAL URL ===
AC1 page renders app name + build identifier — PASS. HTTP 200. Rendered body innerText verbatim: 'MyGame\n\nBuild: 4194c8c'. document.title 'MyGame'. h1 count=1, text 'MyGame'. [data-testid=build-id] visible=true, textContent 'Build: 4194c8c', computed {display:block, visibility:visible, opacity:1, color:rgb(0,0,0), fontSize:16px, w:1216, h:18}. 0 pageerrors, 0 requestfailed. Screenshot captured (desktop + mobile).

AC2 /api/health 200 with identifier MATCHING the page — PASS. Fetched from INSIDE the loaded browser session: HTTP 200, body verbatim {"status":"ok","buildId":"4194c8c"}, page 4194c8c === api 4194c8c, MATCH. Plus 6 paired cache-busted curl runs, all MATCH, with page served x-vercel-cache: HIT (prerendered) and api x-vercel-cache: MISS (dynamic) on every single pair — two different serving mechanisms, still in agreement. The sprint's named risk does not reproduce.

AC3 deployed identifier corresponds to the commit shipped — PASS, same nuance as round 1. last_shipped_commit fe7f2db, live buildId 4194c8c. Re-verified: git diff fe7f2db..4194c8c touches exactly one file, docs/sprints/state/sprint-1.json (+24/-6); diff excluding docs/sprints is EMPTY, so application code is byte-identical to the audited commit. 4194c8c is tip of both local and remote main. Not a stale build.

=== PROCESS NOTE ON MY OWN EVIDENCE ===
My first pass at the curl-side page extractor returned an empty build id on all 5 runs and briefly looked like a page-vs-API mismatch. It was MY regex, not a defect: the markup is 'data-testid="build-id">Build: <code>4194c8c', and a <code> element sits between the label and the SHA, which 'Build: [a-z0-9]*' cannot span. I inspected the raw HTML, corrected the extractor, and re-ran 6 clean paired runs. Recording this so nobody later finds the discarded run and reads it as a real signal.

=== ROBUSTNESS / BREAK ATTEMPTS — ALL HELD ===
- 3 runs in FRESH browser contexts (cold cache, cache-busted): innerText identical all 3, 'MyGame\n\nBuild: 4194c8c', 0 pageerrors each.
- 4 consecutive hard reloads: innerText unchanged all 4, cumulative pageerrors 0.
- Methods on /api/health: GET 200, HEAD 200, POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH all 405. Correct. (PATCH is new this round, round 1 did not test it.)
- Unknown routes: /no-such-page 404, /api/nope 404. Browser-rendered 404 page innerText: '404\nThis page could not be found.'
- Mobile 390x844: scrollWidth 390 === clientWidth 390, no horizontal overflow, innerText identical to desktop.
- HTTPS enforced, strict-transport-security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload.

=== NON-BLOCKING, CARRIED FORWARD ===
2. [LOW] /favicon.ico and /apple-touch-icon.png both still 404. Exactly one console error on every page load, verbatim: 'Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 ()'. It is the only console noise on the page.
3. [INFO] Second Vercel project 'mygame1' reportedly hooked to this repo (from Pipeman round 1, still not independently verified by me — outside browser scope).

RECOMMENDATION: Unchanged from round 1, and re-running the test did not and could not change it. Dev Team fixes two lines (README.md:3, CLAUDE.md:319), Pipeman re-ships, I re-verify. The deployed application itself needs no change — it held under every attempt I made to break it, across two independent test rounds.
